title: numidlabs/wazn-2b-v0.1 · Hugging Face
excerpt: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
content_html:
Wazn is a decision model: given a context, optional rules and an instruction, it returns a probability distribution over a set of labels you supply, each with an optional definition and few-shot examples. Nothing is generated.

Experimental. For trying the model out, not for production.

How it works

  1. Encode each candidate. The rules, context and instruction are followed by one candidate label (its definition and examples), closed by a </choice> tag. The frozen Qwen3.5-2B backbone, with LoRA adapters, reads this sequence, and the hidden state at </choice> is projected into a representation of that candidate.
  2. Compare the candidates. A relational judge compares the candidate representations against each other, rather than scoring each label alone, and outputs a probability for each one.
  3. Check that any label fits. A NONE gate estimates the probability that at least one candidate is valid. Below a threshold the answer is NONE; otherwise it is the most likely candidate.

Use

Python 3.11+. Install the wazn-experimental package in a virtual environment, then start a local server with this checkpoint:

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install --pre "wazn-experimental[server]"
wazn-experimental serve --model numidlabs/wazn-2b-v0.1
# serving on http://127.0.0.1:8000
  • --pre is needed while the package only has alpha releases (0.1.0aN).
  • Keep the quotes around "wazn-experimental[server]"; zsh treats the brackets as a glob.
  • [server] installs PyTorch (a large download). On Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, use "wazn-experimental[server,cuda]" for the fast kernels.

Then query it from Python:

from wazn_experimental import Client, Request, Instruction, Label

request = Request(
    context="My running shoes arrived in the wrong size. Can I swap them?",
    instructions=[Instruction(
        "Which team should handle this?",
        labels=[Label("returns", "Exchanges, refunds, wrong or damaged items"),
                Label("shipping", "Delivery status, delays, lost packages"),
                Label("billing", "Charges, invoices, payment problems")],
    )],
)
print(Client().predict(request).answer)

Model

  • Backbone: Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B-Base at revision b1485b2fa6dfa1287294f269f5fb618e03d52d7c, loaded from the hub (not in this repo)
  • This repo: the head (43,214,082 parameters: relational judge, NONE gate, tag embeddings, LoRA adapters)
